ORDER 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जनवरी 24, 2026/माघ 4, 1947 535 


1. This is a complaint filed by the complainant u/s 33A of the Industrial Disputes Act 1947 raising the 
following contentions: - 


The complainant was appointed by the opposite party in the post of MCS / Office Assistant (Multipurpose) / 
Substaff at their Hunsur branch on 10.12.2004. He submitted application and documents and attended interview for 
selection. Since then he worked continuously in the said branch till the date of his termination / retrenchment / 
discharge / dismissal of his service on 20.10.2016. As a part of his job, he used to open the branch by collecting keys 
from the Manager, cleaning the office, aiding the customers and the branch in various ways. In order to avoid the 
extension of status and benefits of permanent workman to him, the Opposite Party directed the Hunsur branch to debit 
his wages as coolie charges to the General ledger account without obtaining his signature on the debit vouchers. The 
officials of the branch took his signature on the overleaf of coolie paid debit vouchers along with the signatures of the 
branch officers while paying wages in cash to him. He was the only person doing the work of the office attendant / 
messenger / sweeper / substaff / daily wager / MCS etc on coolie charges. The Opposite Party was not marking 
attendance register for his work, not extended payment register to him, signing debit vouchers for his wages by the 
officers of the bank and receiving amount by them and then paying the amounts to him as wages, debiting the wages 
paid to him to General Charges Account instead of salary paid account / Establishment charges, not issuing 
appointment orders or certificates for the services rendered by him in the bank, refusal to pay wages applicable to 
messengers / housekeeping staff / sub staff / MCS to him, not extending the service benefits applicable to permanent 
workman, taking work from him for years together as Coolie by terming his wages as coolie charges practiced by the 
opposite party are all unfair labour practices under the 5" Schedule of the ID Act 1947. The complainant along with 
other coolie workers of the opposite party bank formed a union called Pragathi Grameena Bank Daily Wage Workers 
Union in 2012 and he was active in the Union activities. The Union filed cases before the Central Labour Machinery 
for getting the benefits for the daily wage workers of the Bank. This has caused annoyance to the then management 
against him. CR 15/2015 is pending before this Tribunal in which the Union raised a dispute for regularization of 
services of the workmen including him. He is directly connected with the said dispute and his name appears at 91. No. 
34 in the list of workers. On 20.10.2016, the Branch Manager Mrs. S M Mamatha asked the complainant to work 
under a contractor Gajamukha Agencies in the Bank and on failure his service would be terminated. The complainant 
was not ready to work under a contractor and hence his services are terminated. No other reasons are told by the 
Manager for the termination for his services. Before retrenching his services, the opposite party has not issued any 
notice to him, nor paid any retrenchment compensation, nor paid wages for one month nor conducted any enquiry 
against him. His repeated requests to allow him to do work in the branch were not considered by the Branch Manager. 
The opposite party has not filed any application before the appropriate Government seeking permission to retrench 
him u/s 25 N of the ID Act 1947. Therefore, the retrenchment of his service is illegal, ab-initio void and he is deemed 
to be in the services of the Bank as per sec 25 N(7) of the ID Act. As per the provision of Sec 33 of the ID Act, the 
opposite party cannot alter or change the conditions of his service applicable to him immediately before the 
commencement of the proceedings of C R 15/2015 to his prejudice , during the pendency of CR 15/2015 before this 
Tribunal without the expressed permission in writing from the tribunal and also shall not discharge / dismiss / 
terminate / retrench him unless he was paid wages for one month and without making an application for approval of 
the action so taken. The opposite party has not observed any of the provisions of the ID Act 1947 and has not filed 
any application before the Tribunal. The action of the opposite party is against the provisions of the ID Act, principles 
of natural justice, illegal, null and void. The opposite party was paying him wages @ Rs. 7368/- per month. The 
opposite party has not paid any wages to him since the retrenchment of his services. Since the opposite party has not 
filed any application before the Tribunal seeking approval of their action, he is entitled for payment of full wages 
drawn by him every month till the disposal of this case. Since the opposite party has not filed any application before 
the appropriate government for the termination of his services, not issued any copy of such application to him nor any 
notice / notice pay / compensation as required u/s 25 N of the ID Act, he is deemed to be in service for the benefits as 
applicable to him prior to such cessation of his service and is entitled for wages as per sec 25N (7) of the ID Act. Due 
to the illegal cessation of service imposed on him by the opposite party, the complainant and his family are suffering 
economically and socially. Hence this complaint for declaring the termination / retrenchment / discharge / dismissal 
of the complainant from 20.10.2016 is not in accordance with the provisions of the ID Act 1947, against the principles 
of natural justice, arbitrary, unilateral, ill motivated and illegal and to direct the opposite party to reinstate the 
complainant with full back wages, continuity of service with regularization, ancillary benefits from 20.10.2016 and 
with cost. 


2 The opposite party at the outset has contended that the complainant has no enforceable cause of action to 
raise Industrial Dispute and has no right to seek employment in the bank and there is no discharge or termination of 
employment and hence no Industrial Dispute lie under Industrial Disputes Act 1947. It is equally contended that there 
is no post of messenger cum sweeper in the bank. The opposite party inter alia contended that based on the man 
power requirement assessed by the bank as per the guidelines issued by the Government of India at the end of March 
every year, the total vacancies to be filled up by the direct recruitment and promotions will be identified and the 
process of direct recruitment and promotions will be initiated after obtaining permissions from the Sponsor Bank viz., 
Canara Bank and the Board of the opposite party bank. Recruitment and appointment of employees in the Regional 
Rural Banks is governed by the rules framed by the Government of India vide notification dated 13.07.2010 called 


536 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JANUARY 24, 2026/MAGHA 4, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


“Regional Rural Banks (Appointment and Promotions of Officers and Employees) Rules 2010”. As per the said rules, 
procedure with regard to Office Attendant (Multipurpose Group C employees) are prescribed, the selection process 
being on the basis of interview to be conducted by a Committee. The branches / offices of the bank engage coolies 
occasionally and intermittently as and when necessitated for doing menial works in the branches. In order to meet the 
exigencies of the work, the opposite party bank branches used to engage coolies only for few hours for such menial 
works like cleaning, sweeping and watering and were paid coolie charges proportionately depending upon the number 
of hours they worked. The complainant was also engaged similarly as a coolie intermittently and not continuously. 
Depending upon the availability of the person in the locale, the Branch Manager engaged such person on need basis 
for such works. As per the Government of India guidelines for appointment of Regular Attendants, the names should 
be sponsored by the employment exchange and such engagement is also subject to the conditions stipulated in regard 
to educational qualification, age etc. While engaging the coolies, no educational qualifications or age were looked into 
and whoever is available would be engaged. The persons so engaged are at liberty to work elsewhere after completion 
of the menial works entrusted to them. They are not governed by any rules and regulation of the bank and there is no 
employee employer relationship as they have not been engaged by the bank against the post. It is the settled position 
in law that a person engaged intermittently on daily wages will not have the right to be absorbed for any post. The 
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Karnataka vs. Uma Devi held that there is no right to those who have 
been engaged as daily wagers temporarily or on contractual basis to claim that they have the right to be absorbed in 
service as they cannot be said to be holders of post. In Union of India vs. A $ Pillai also the Hon'ble Supreme Court 
held that daily wager / part time workers not engaged in any regular cadres or any sanctioned post are not entitled for 
absorption. The contention of the complainant that he was appointed by the opposite party at their Hunsur branch on 
10.12.2004 by taking application form etc. is denied. The Branch Manager has no power to recruit / appoint any 
employee. The complainant was engaged only occasionally to attend to menial / urgent works and not continuously. 
Since the complainant was not recruited / appointed by the opposite party anytime, his termination / dismissal / 
retrenchment on 20.10.2016 did not arise. Consequently, question of issuing notice to him, payment of retrenchment 
compensation, payment of wages of one month, filing of application before the Tribunal before or during the 
pendency of CR 15/2015 and seeking permission u/s 25N of the Act does not arise. Under the circumstances, sec 33 
of the Industrial Disputes Act has no application in his case. He was never engaged for attending the regular functions 
of substaff. He was paid wages for the occasional / casual works he was engaged to. The Branch Managers are not 
authorized to issue any certificates and question of issuing certificates to him does not arise as he was not 
continuously engaged in the opposite party bank and nor was empanelled in the daily wagers’ list. The complainant 
has not been appointed in the payrolls of the opposite party at any time. Since he has not been appointed in the 
opposite party bank, question of marking in the attendance register, extending payment registered to him, debiting the 
payment made to him to salary account, issuing appointment orders, issuing certificates and denying benefits etc. did 
not arise. Hence the allegation of unfair labour practice on the part of the II Party is untenable. The contention of the 
complainant that his involvement in the union activities and filing of Industrial Dispute by the said union for getting 
benefits to the daily wage workers has caused anger to the opposite party is a figment of his imagination and hence 
denied. The complainant was not working in the opposite party bank on continuous basis and was engaged 
occasionally, casually for menial and urgent requirements. His contention that he was being paid wages @ Rs. 7368/- 
is denied. His contentions that he was deemed to be in service and entitled for benefits are untenable and baseless. 
The complainant has not undergone any process of recruitment and is not entitled for recruitment for appointment in 
the opposite party bank or for reinstatement or other ancillary benefits as claimed by him. For all these reasons, the 
opposite party has prayed for rejection of the complaint. 


3. From the above rival pleadings, following points arise for consideration:- 

1. Whether the complaint is legally and factually maintainable? 

2. Whether the Complainant is proved to have been working continuously in the opposite party establishment 
since 10.12.2004? 

3. Whether the complainant is proved to have been discharged / terminated / retrenched / dismissed from 
service as contended by him? 

4. Whether the alleged contravention of the provision of sec 33 of the ID Act is proved by the complainant? 

5. Whether the complainant is entitled to get reinstatement to the service with full back wages, continuity of 
service and ancillary benefits from 20.10.2016 as prayed for? 

6. What is the proper Order and Award to be passed in this complaint case? 

4. Either of the parties did not prefer to adduce any evidence in the matter. Though the complainant is seen to 


have filed an affidavit dated 07.01.2021 in lieu of his examination in chief and sought time for further examination in 
chief, he did not thenceforth prefer to make him available for further examination in chief or cross-examination. 


5. Heard the oral and written arguments submitted from both sides. 


6. Points no. 1 to 4:- Since all these points are closely integrated and inter-twined, all these points are 
discussed together. Alleging contravention of the provisions of sec 33 of the ID Act 1947, the complainant filed the 
instant complaint u/s 33A of the Act on the factual averment that the opposite party has not filed any application 


[भाग --खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जनवरी 24, 2026/माघ 4, 1947 537 


before this Tribunal seeking permission for retrenching / terminating / dismissing him on 20.10.2016 and not filing 
any application for approval of their said action. The complainant’s case is that he was appointed by the opposite 
party bank at their Hunsur branch on 10.12.2004 on submission of application and subjecting him for interview and 
on obtaining documents from him. He claims that since then he has worked continuously in the said branch on all 
working days. It is his further case that on 20.10.2014, the then Branch Manager asked him to work under a contractor 
Gajamukha Agencies and in the event he does not heed to that, not to come for work anymore and eventually he 
services are terminated by the opposite party as he was not ready to work under a contractor. This particular averment, 
the opposite party emphatically disputed. The complainant inter alia pleaded that he is an active member in a Union 
under the name and style Pragathi Grameena Bank Daily Wage Workers Union formed between himself with other 
coolie workers of the opposite party bank. The said union has raised a dispute for regularization of the service of the 
complainant and other similarly placed coolie before the Central Government Machinery and the same is registered 
and pending before this Tribunal as CR 15/2015. It is the case of the complainant that he is directly connected with 
the said dispute raised by the Union pending before this Tribunal. The disengagement of job on 20.10.2016 according 
to the complainant tantamounts to contravention of the provisions of sec 33 of the ID Act as according to him, it 
happened when the industrial dispute raised by the union for and on behalf of him and the other coolie workers was 
pending adjudication. This gave way for filing this complaint u/s 33A of the ID Act. 


7. Oral and written arguments are advanced on behalf of the complainant narrating all these events by his 
authorized representative. 


8. The learned counsel for the opposite party per contra put forth his rival submission that the complainant has 
never ever rendered any continuous service in the opposite party bank. Instead the bank was in the practice of 
engaging persons from the locale for attending menial job like sweeping, cleaning and watering whenever so 
necessitated and such persons were paid coolie charges for the same. According to the opposite party, the complainant 
was also so casually engaged occasionally and intermittently depending on the requirement of the branch as a coolie 
for doing menial works and such works carried out by him was not regular in nature, but only on need basis. 


9. Of course, the event of non-engagement for work said to have happened on 20.10.2016 is apparently during 
the pendency of CR 15/2015. However the complainant did not prefer to bring home any proof that he was in service 
in the opposite party bank even on the previous day or anytime there-before in a constant and continuous stretch so as 
to establish the retrenchment / dismissal / discharge / termination alleged in the complaint. Here it is contextually 
profitable to quote Sec 33 of the Act:- 


33. [ Conditions of service, etc., to remain unchanged under certain circumstances during pendency of 
proceedings. ] 


(1)During the pendency of any conciliation proceeding before a conciliation officer or a Board or of any 
proceeding before ][an arbitrator or] [a Labour Court or Tribunal or National Tribunal in respect of an 
industrial dispute, no employer shall- (a)in regard to any matter connected with the dispute, alter, to the 
prejudice of the workmen concerned in such dispute, the conditions of service applicable to them immediately 
before the commencement of such proceeding; or (b)for any misconduct connected with the dispute, discharge 
or punish, whether by dismissal or otherwise, any workmen concerned in such dispute, ave with the express 
permission in writing of the authority before which the proceeding is pending.(2)During the pendency of any 
such proceeding in respect of an industrial dispute, the employer may, in accordance with the standing orders 
applicable to a workman concerned in such dispute ] [or, where there are no such standing orders, in 
accordance with the terms of the contract, whether express or implied, between him and the workman] (a)[ 
alter, in regard to any matter not connected with the dispute, the conditions of service applicable to that 
workman immediately before the commencement of such proceeding; or (b) for any misconduct not connected 
with the dispute, discharge or punish, whether by dismissal or otherwise, that workman: Provided that no such 
workman shall be discharged or dismissed, unless he has been paid wages for one month and an application 
has been made by the employer to the authority before which the proceeding is pending for approval of the 
action taken by the employer. (3)Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), no employer shall, 
during the pendency of any such proceeding in respect of an industrial dispute, take any action against any 
protected workman concerned in such dispute (a) by altering, to the prejudice of such protected workman, the 
conditions of service applicable to him immediately before the commencement of such proceedings; or (b) by 
discharging or punishing, whether by dismissal or otherwise, such protected workman, save with the express 
permission in writing of the authority before which the proceeding is pending. Explanation:-For the purposes of 
this sub-section, a "protected workman ", in relation to an establishment, means a workman who, being] [a 
member of the executive or other office bearer] [of a registered trade union connected with the establishment, is 
recognised as such in accordance with rules made in this behalf.(4)In every establishment, the number of 
workmen to be recognised as protected workmen for the purposes of sub-section (3) shall be one per cent. of the 
total number of workmen employed therein subject to a minimum number of five protected workmen and a 
maximum number of one hundred protected workmen and for the aforesaid purpose, the appropriate 
Government may make rules providing for the distribution of such protected workmen among various trade 
unions, if any, connected with the establishment and the manner in which the workmen may be chosen and 


538 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JANUARY 24, 2026/MAGHA 4, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


recognised as protected workmen.(5)Where an employer makes an application to a conciliation officer, Board, 
] [an arbitrator, a] [Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal under the proviso to sub-section (2) for 
approval of the action taken by him, the authority concerned shall, without delay, hear such application and 
pass, ] [within a period of three months from the date of receipt of such application] [ Substituted by Act 46_of 
1982, Section 17, for " as expeditiously as possible" (w.e.f. 21.8.1984).][, such order in relation thereto as it 
deems fit:]. ][Provided that where any such authority considers it necessary or expedient so to do, it may, for 
reasons to be recorded in writing, extend such period by such further period as it may think fit: Provided 
further that no proceedings before any such authority shall lapse merely on the ground that any period 
specified in this sub-section had expired without such proceedings being completed. ] 


10. Of course by enacting sec 33, the legislature wanted to ensure a fair and satisfactory enquiry of the industrial 
dispute undisturbed by any action on the part of the employer or the employee likely to create fresh cause for 
disharmony between them. The legislature visualized that during the pendency of the industrial dispute status quo 
should be maintained and no further element of discord should be introduced between the employer and the 
employee. The objective of the provision of sec 33 is to put a ban on the prerogative of the employer in altering the 
service condition of the employee pending enquiry of the industrial dispute raised by them. The primary principle is 
that if an Industrial Dispute is raised by a group of workmen acting on their own through their union, the general 
conclusion is that the all those who sponsored the dispute are concerned in it. However the very factum of raising an 
Industrial Dispute and pendency of such a dispute in a court of law by an individual employee or a group of 
employees by itself does not lead to the inference that such an individual who alleges retrenchment from services was 
a workman in continuous service under the employer, unless proved by concrete evidence. Indeed, Sec 33A stands to 
the rescue of a workman who alleges alteration or cessation of service by the employer during the pendency of an 
Industrial Dispute. A regular workman / employee or a casual employee on a continuing basis under an employer who 
files a complaint u/s 33A certainly stands on a different footing than the one who claims continuity of service as a 
casual labourer and whose claim is not accepted by the employer. 


11. The case on hand portrays the scenario the employer disowns and denies the complainant as its regular daily 
wager. The alleged retrenchment of service dated 20.10.2016 averred by the complainant is not accepted or 
recognized by the Oppose Party in the given case. The definite stand of the opposite party is that the complainant had 
been engaged very occasionally and intermittently on need basis to attend menial works like sweeping, cleaning etc. 
without touching the routine works in the office. The complainant per contra very particularly pleaded that apart from 
cleaning in and around the bank office, he was entrusted with the task of assisting customers in making challans for 
cash / cheque, deposits taking and keeping cash in double lock, writing registers, collecting cash from other banks 
from the cheques drawn on them, printing passbooks, deposit receipts, writing loan papers, making deposit 
mobilization, bundling payment slips and day book and such so many tasks. However according to the opposite party 
all the above works are the routine tasks of the regular employees and not of such casual workers engaged for 
attending menial jobs. Thus the factual pleadings of the complainant indicate that his engagement in the opposite 
party bank was not to attend menial labour alone but higher tasks as well, as mentioned above. It is while attending 
such highly responsible tasks in his so called status as MCS / Office assistant (multipurpose) / sub-staff at the Hunsur 
branch of the opposite party continuously since 10.12.2004 that the opposite party has terminated / retrenched his 
services on 20.10.2016. This factum also the opposite party has emphatically opposed and disputed. According to the 
opposite party, no such retrenchment or termination has ever occurred nor was there any occasion for that as the bank 
had not engaged the complainant in such a position at all in work continuously. In this factual background it is the 
primary duty of the complainant to substantiate that his very entry in the bank was on 10.12.2004 and he continued to 
perform services in the opposite party bank without any break till 20.10.2016. The complainant is equally obliged to 
prove that he was disengaged from a continuous service on 20.10.2016. Inability to offer menial job on a particular 
date when there was no requirement to engage a casual labourer to attend such work pleaded by the opposite party 
does oblige the complainant to substantiate his specific case by adducing reliable and concrete material evidence 
establishing all the aspects pleaded by him in the complaint. The mere pleading raised by him regarding the 
prevalence / pendency of an Industrial Dispute and the so called termination or retrenchment of services on 
20.10.2016 without bringing home any iota of evidence substantiating the above plea does not bind this Tribunal to 
accept the case set forth by him as gospel truth and to draw a finding against the opposite party. 


12. It is the settled position of law that u/s 33A of the Industrial Disputes Act, the complainant carries the initial 
burden / onus to prove that the employer contravened sec 33 of the Act and such contravention occurred during the 
pendency of a dispute, by presenting the facts supported by evidence. Once the complainant discharges his initial 
burden to establish that he is an employee in continuous service within the parameters of sec 33 of the Act and such 
contravention occurred as pleaded and proved, the employer must then justify their actions especially concerning 
alleged dismissal / retrenchment / termination, often leading to the tribunal deciding if the action was fair and just like 
any other Industrial Dispute. 


13. Here in the given case, the one and only aspect accepted and admitted by the opposite party is the pendency 
of CR 15/2015 raised by the Daily Workers Union. That by itself does not discharge the onus of proof cast on the 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जनवरी 24, 2026/माघ 4, 1947 539 


complainant to prima facie establish its case. The alleged contravention of service conditions or an illegal cessation of 
the service of an employee by the employer is not an aspect to be simply inferred by the Tribunal out of nothing but to 
be very precisely, meticulously and scrupulously proved and established by the aggrieved complainant. 


14. Sec 33A is designed to provide an instant remedy to a workman aggrieved by the contravention of sec 33 by 
filing a complaint before adjudicatory authorities or conciliatory authorities. It is trite that where such a complaint is 
made to an adjudicatory authority viz. Labour Court / Tribunal, it will adjudicate upon the dispute as if it is a dispute 
referred to or pending before it, so that the workman is saved of the botheration of moving the Government for 
referring this dispute for adjudication. 


15. The basic question to be considered by this Tribunal in the complaint on hand u/s 33A is whether there has 
been a contravention by the employer of the provisions of sec 33 and in the event it is found that there has been a 
contravention of the provisions, then to embark upon the exercise to adjudicate about the matter so complained of in 
the complaint on its merit. No written order of termination / retrenchment is produced by the complainant to justify 
his pleadings. Of course, he averred in the complaint that the termination issued by the opposite party was only oral. 
If that be so, it should be proved by the complainant that he was in continuous service under the opposite party and 
was subjected for a termination / retrenchment on an oral order by mounting the witness box. Going by the 
proceedings underwent in the given case, it is clear that once the statement of objection is filed by the opposite party, 
the matter was posted for evidence of the complainant. The latter though filed an affidavit dated 07.01.2021 in lieu of 
his examination in chief and sought time for further examination in chief, he did not thenceforth prefer to make 
himself available for further examination in chief or cross-examination. Then at the whimsical stand of the 
complainant it is made out that there is no need to adduce evidence and the matter be posted for arguments. In fact, as 
per law, before giving any relief to the aggrieved employee under the section, the authority viz., this Tribunal has first 
to determine that the employee was continuously working under the employer and the latter had surreptitiously kicked 
out him from the job without complying with the mandate u/s 33 of the Act. Hence a contravention of sec 33 is the 
foundation for exercise of the power u/s 33A of the Act. As already observed and as rightly pointed out by the learned 
counsel for the opposite party, no reliable proof / evidence is brought on record by the complainant to substantiate that 
there is contravention of the provisions of sec 33 of the Act from the side of the opposite party. 


16. In the event if the alleged factum of infraction from the provision of sec 33 is established, the matter has to 
be very meticulously adjudicated on merit to examine whether the complainant is entitled to get an order of 
reinstatement. It is trite that even when contravention of sec 33 is established, that does not automatically lead to an 
order for reinstatement. So, at large, the complainant is at the task to prove and establish the primary elements viz., 
his status as a daily wage employee under the opposite party coupled with contravention of the provisions of sec 33 
by the latter and then his eventual right to get reinstatement to service with equivalent benefits. Determination of all 
these issues by the legal forum could be possible only when reliable evidence is adduced by the complainant by 
offering himself for searching cross examination by the opposite party in a full-fledged trial. It is trite that the initial 
burden lies on the employee to prove that he falls under the definition of a “workman” under the Industrial Disputes 
Act. If the employee presents a strong prima facie case, the management must then provide evidence to rebut it. Of 
course, the evidence to be adduced by the person claiming to be an employee must be substantial, often a 
preponderance of evidence depending on the claim. It is no longer res-integra that the burden of proving the 
employer-employee relationship primarily rest upon the person who asserts its existence. In a situation where a person 
asserts to be an employee of the management which the management denies, the duty primarily rests upon the person 
so asserting to give positive evidence in his favour and discharge his initial burden. At the risk of repetition I say, 
once such a person has given such a positive evidence in his favour, only then the burden would shift on the 
management to give evidence to counter such claims, because it is always possible to prove positive facts than a 
negative. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Workman of Nilgiri Co-Op Mkt Society LTD vs. State of Tamil Nadu 
(AIR 2004 SC 1639) held that it is a well settled principle of law that the person who is setting up a plea of existence 
of relationship of employer and employee, the burden would be upon him. Similar view is adopted by the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court in Bank of Baroda vs. Ghemarabhai Harijibhai Rabari (2005 (10) SCC 792). Though the 
complainant is seen to have filed an affidavit dated 07.01.2021 in lieu of his examination in chief and sought time for 
further examination in chief, he did not thenceforth prefer to make him available for further examination in chief or 
cross-examination and thereby kept aloof from trial, feeling shy of an intensive quiz in the witness box. Probably, the 
complainant might have been misled, misguided or mal-advised not to mount the witness box so as to avoid probable 
inconvenience of a grilling cross-examination. The net result of such willful avoidance of requisite procedure by the 
complainant either by himself or as instilled upon him is complete failure of the case projected by him. 


17. Extensive argument is advanced on behalf of the complainant with the aid of plethora of legal authorities 
canvassing for a favorable order of reinstatement with full back wages, continuity of service with regularization and 
ancillary benefits from 20.10.2016. As could be heard from Learned Counsel for the opposite party, all these wider 
reliefs sought for by the complainant are the main reliefs claimed in the said case CR 15/2015. By consciously 
avoiding to give oral or documentary evidence in this case, what is craved for and on behalf of the complainant is to 
grant the above reliefs even without facing a trial. Granting such reliefs in his favour without providing / 


540 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JANUARY 24, 2026/MAGHA 4, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


supplementing any sort of evidentiary support would tantamount to prejudging the issue raised in the Industrial 
Dispute case CR 15/2015 in a very shortcut method. 


18. Argument is advanced on behalf of the complainant placing reliance upon the verdicts of the Hon'ble High 
Court of Gujarat in Gujarat State Electricity Corporation LTD vs. Bhimrao Aagete (LPA 177 / 2016 dated 
06.03.2018), Kalavatiben Prabhakar Patil and others vs. Managing Director (C/SCA/3189/2020 dated 
17.01.2022) that while deciding a complaint u/s 33A it is not obligatory for the workman to prove that he had worked 
for 240 days. Those rulings in fact do not indicate that the complainant is not at all under obligation to substantiate his 
basic status under the opposite party to justify the case put forth. 


19. In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and the very casual manner in which it is manned by the 
complainant, the plethora of rulings relied upon by him viz., Hindustan Lever LTD vs. Ram Mohan Roy and 
others (AIR 1973 SC 1156) by the Hon'ble Apex Court, Management of Karur Vysya Bank LTD vs. Presiding 
Officer, Industrial Tribunal (2007 IT LLJ 459) by the Hon'ble High Court of Madras, M M Narayana vs. KSRTC 
(AIR 2012 (4) KAR R 518) and Karan Kumar vs. Divisional Controller KSRTC (WP 203333/2019 dated 
13.07.2023) by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and Deutsche Lufthansa AG vs. Nayan Pahwa & others 
(2025 INSC 998) by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi are not of any help to the complainant as in all those cases non- 
compliance of the provisions by the respective employers are relating to regular employees on its payroll. Among the 
cases noted above, the case of Karur Vysya Bank LTD, MM Narayana and Karan Kumar are related to the 
actions initiated by the respective employers based on misconduct / misdemeanor of the respective regular employees 
in respect of which approval applications were not submitted by the employers. In Hindustan Lever’s case also, the 
complainants were the regular employees of the employer establishment. In principle, the fact situations contained in 
the afore-quoted ruling do not have any application to the case on hand. 


20. Before concluding, it is worthy to pen down that in order to avail the relief provided u/s 33 of the Act, firstly 
the aggrieved party should prove himself to be a workman within the definition of u/s 2(s) of the Industrial Disputes 
Act and there exists employer-employee relationship between the contesting parties. In conclusion of the afore- 
discussion, I find that the complainant has miserably failed in substantiating his own case. He equally failed in 
refuting / negating the contentions raised by the opposite party that he is only a coolie engaged on need and 
requirement basis without continuity and frequency and hence not governed by any rules and regulations of the bank. 
So also, the complainant further failed in successfully controverting the rival contentions of the opposite party that 
there is no employee-employer relationship between himself and the opposite party or that he was not engaged by the 
latter against a sanctioned post. The deliberate refusal, negligence or avoidance to prove and establish a genuine and 
reliable case by tendering requisite evidence has led the complainant to face a total failure in the given case and for an 
eventual dismissal of the complaint. With this view, these points are answered accordingly. 


21. Point No. 5:- In view of the findings on point no. 1 10 4, it is held that the complainant is not entitled for any 
reliefs sought for in this complaint. 


22. Point no. 6:- In the result the following award is passed. 
AWARD 
The Complaint no. 03/2017 is dismissed.

Present:- Sh. Arun Batra, AR for workman. 
Sh. Tarun Dhingra, AR for respondent no.1 to 3. 

Central Government vide Notification No. L-12012/05/2015-IR(B-D Dated 03.02.2015, under clause (d) of 
sub-section (1) and sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (hereinafter called the Act), 
has referred the following Industrial dispute for adjudication to this Tribunal:- 

“Whether the action of the management of Serve Haryana Gramin Bank (formerly known as Gurgaon 

Gramin Bank), Gurgaon in terminating the services of Shri Devender S/o Late Shri Om Parkash 

w.ef. 05.12.2013 is valid, just and legal? If not to what relief the concerned workman is entitled to and 


from which date?” 


1. Both the parties were served with notices. The workman filed his statement of claim with the averment that 
he was appointed as Peon by the respondents/managements on 21.09.2010 at the payment of Rs.280/- per day with 


542 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JANUARY 24, 2026/MAGHA 4, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


respondent no.3. Respondents had not provided any appointment letter, PF, ESI Card or any other documents by 
using unfair labour practice. The respondents has obtained workman’s signature on some printed documents by 
stating that it shall be used as a record of service. The record of the workman relating to his salary is reserved in the 
contingency account section of respondent which is available with the respondents. The workman rendered his 
services with utmost honesty without any complaint but in spite of that, management began to harass the workman 
when the name of Gurgaon Gramin Bank is changed as Serve Haryana Gramin Bank. Ultimately, against the 
provision of Section 25-F of the Industrial Dispute Act, management retrenched the services of the workman on 
05.12.2013 without any enquiry or without giving any retrenchment compensation while he had worked more than 
240 days on each calendar year before his retrenchment. Workman worked from 21.09.2010 upto 2013 in Dasuya, 
Faridabad Branch under the Manager ML Aggarwal. The workman moved an application before the Assistant 
Labour Commissioner (Central) Karnal for conciliation but of no result. The workman is unemployed from the date 
of retrenchment till date. It is therefore, prayed that workman be ordered to be reappointed with all benefits with 
continuous service. 


2. Respondent 10.1 to 3 has filed its written statement, alleging therein that petition moved by 
claimant/workman is not maintainable because there is no Industrial Dispute between the parties. The workman was 
a daily wager and engaged for a day and the services of the workman starts from morning and come to an end in the 
evening. The workman was never engaged as daily worker for regular work. The engagement of the workman was 
not under any recruitment process. The workman was engaged as daily wager by erstwhile Gurgaon Gramin Bank. 
The Gurgaon Gramin Bank with its Head Office at Gurgaon and erstwhile Haryana Gramin Bank with its Head 
Office at Rohtak have been amalgamated and a new entity has come into being know as Sarva Haryana Gramin 
Bank vide Notification dated 29.11.2013 of Govt. of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services, 
New Delhi. After the amalgamation, respondent-management of Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank did not engage the 
workman because his hiring as daily wager not under the prescribed lawful recruitment process as provided in the 
Regional Rural Banks (Appointment and Promotion of Officers and Employees) Rules, 2010. In view of the facts 
and circumstances mentioned above, it is therefore, respectfully prayed that the case of the workman may kindly be 
dismissed with heavy costs, being devoid of merits in the interest of justice. 


3. Parties were given opportunity to lead evidence. 


4. The workman has examined himself as WW1 and filed his affidavit in evidence as Ex.WW1/A along with 
documents Ex.W-1 bearing page 10.1 to 38 and has been cross-examined by the AR for respondents. AR for 
workman closed the evidence on 12.02.2020. 


Ds The respondents have filed affidavit of Sh. Rajinder Kumar Goyal, Senior Manager, Sarva Haryana Gramin 
Bank, who filed his affidavit in evidence as Ex.MWI1/A along with documents MW1/1 (Reply dated 13.03.2025) 
and Ex.MW1/2 (Email received from Head Office dated 17.03.2025) and has been cross-examined by the learned 
AR of workman. AR for respondents closed the evidence on 19.03.2025. 


6. The workman filed written arguments, alleging therein that he was appointed as Peon on 21.09.2010 in the 
office of Manager of Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank (previously known as Gurgaon Gramin Bank) at Branch NIT 
Faridabad. The workman was drawing a salary of Rs.280/- per day from the management. The workman was 
granted TA, DA for his travel allowance by the management. The management violated the provisions of the Act 
and did not supply appointment letter, PF account number, ESI card to the workman. The management got sign from 
the workman on plain papers on the pretext of using these papers for the service record and workman did sign these 
blank papers on the asking of the officials of the bank as the requirement of the service of the workman. The 
workman did not protest against the official for getting the signatures on the blank papers, being afraid of losing the 
job. The record pertaining to the salary of workman is available with the concerned-branch of the bank in the shape 
of debit slips and contingency account. The work of the workman was satisfactory and at no point of time any 
complaint was made against the work of the workman. On the change of the name of the bank to Sarva Haryana 
Gramin Bank, management started harassing the workman on one pretext or the other. The services of the workman 
were terminated orally on 05.12.2013 without issuing any notice or retrenchment compensation. The workman has 
completed more than 240 days in a calendar year in the employment of the management without any break. The 
work is still available with the management and the workman is no where gainfully employed. The workman filed 
an application for summoning the attendance record, salary record, provident fund details and ESI details of the 
workman but the management failed to supply the record. Adverse inference may kindly be drawn against the 
management for not producing the summoned record. The management paid salary to the workman against 
signatures and receipts. On 28.04.2014, after terminating the services of workman, management advertised 175 post 
of Office Attendant (Multipurpose) Group C whereas workman is available to serve on this post. Workman along 
with others challenged this advertisement before the Hon’ble Punjab & Haryana High Court by filing CWP No.9254 
of 2014 and the Hon’ble High Court directed that in the meanwhile, the applications made by the workmen for the 
above said posts shall be accepted by the respondent-bank subject to the decision of the writ petition. The 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जनवरी 24, 2026/माघ 4, 1947 543 


management decided to withdraw the advertisement dated 28.04.2014 on 26.04.2016 and the said writ petition was 
disposed of as become infructuous. Earlier the management has issued letter dated 25.11.2009 raising requirement 
of Part Time worker for the smooth working of the branch. On 14.09.2010, a letter was issued by the General 
Manger of Gurgaon Gramin Bank directing not to engage a particular person for more than 55 days in continuity and 
to ensure that the person engaged as per point 10.1 mentioned above is not engaged for more that 230 days in a year, 
whereas the workman had worked more than 240 days in many calendar years. On 08.11.2011, a letter was issued to 
the workman by the management to appear for the post of office attendant on 17.11.2011 at 01.00 pm but the 
workman was not allowed to attend the interview for the reason best known to the management. The workman 
applied for the post advertised vide advertisement dated 28.04.2014. During the pendency of the present case, the 
management issued circular dated 23.06.2023, wherein offices/branches has been directed to fix the charges of the 
daily wagers. It is maintained that the workman is entitled to reinstatement with all back wages. 


7. Management has not filed any written argument but has argued orally. It is maintained by the AR for 
management that workman has never completed 240 days in year and was called on the necessity basis on a 
particular day. No record was being maintained by the management of the workman as he was not even part time 
employee and further if the workman was paid through his bank account as alleged by the workman, he should have 
placed on record original record to satisfy his case that he has worked 240 days in a year prior to his termination and 
he has not placed the same. Thus, the reference is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed. 


8. I have heard learned AR for the parties and have gone through the entire evidence placed on file by the 
parties. 
9. There is no dispute about the preposition of law that onus to prove that workman was in the employment of 


management is always on the workman/claimant and it is for the workman to adduce evidence to prove factum of 
his employment with the management. Such evidence may be in the form of receipt of salary of wages for 240 days 
or record of his/her appointment or engagement for that year to show that he/she has worked with the employer for 
240 days or more in a calendar year. In this regard, reference may be made to Batala Coop. Sugar Mills Ltd. Vs. 
Sowaran_Singh(2005) 8 Supreme Court cases 481 as well as Director Fisheries Terminated Division Vs. 
Bhikubhai Meghajibhai Gavda(2012) 1 SCC 47. 


10. In his affidavit Ex.WW1/A the workman has reiterated his case that he was appointed as Peon on 
21.09.2010 in the office of Manager of Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank, previously known as Gurgaon Gramin Bank, at 
Branch NIT Faridabad and used to work for the whole day. He was drawing salary @Rs.280/- per day from the 
management. He had completed more than 240 days in the management without any break and his services were 
terminated orally on 05.12.2013. During his cross-examination, he has admitted that a few times payments were 
made by vouchers and sometime through his bank account. He has no original documents issued by the bank. 


11. It was incumbent upon the workman to prove that he had worked for 240 days preceding the year of his 
alleged termination on 05.12.2013. Except his bald statement, there is nothing on the record to prove that he had 
worked for 240 days with the respondent-bank. Even in his cross-examination, the workman had admitted that a few 
times payments were made by vouchers and sometime through his bank account. He has no original documents from 
the bank. When he was being paid through vouchers and sometime through his bank account, payment made to him 
is surely reflected in his bank account. He has placed on record photocopy of saving bank account in which some 
amount has been credited but it is not clear that the amount credited by the respondent-bank. Similarly he has placed 
on record photocopy of some vouchers and from these vouchers it cannot be said that he has received some payment 
from the bank as these have not been proved by calling some person from the bank. Thus, it cannot be conclusively 
proved that prior to his termination on 05.12.2013 in the preceding year he has worked for 240 days in that year. 
Thus, his bald statement maintaining that he worked from 21.09.2010 to 05.12.2013 is not proved when the 
workman was having best evidence in his possession. 


12. It is added here that workman had moved an application on 23.02.2021 for issuing direction to the 
respondent-bank to place on record the following documents i.e. attendance record, salary record, provident fund 
details and ESI details of the workman. In reply thereto, it is maintained by the management that since the workman 
was only daily wager so the above said record of the workman is not with the respondent as the workman was paid 
through debit voucher. Even in the affidavit of the management witness Sh. Rajinder Kumar Goyal filed as 
Ex.MWI1/A, the management has stated that the workman was engaged for daily basis and was called on daily basis 
on a day from morning and his services ends in the evening on the same day and engagement of the workman was 
for a day. There was no provision of maintaining record or ACR of the workman because his engagement was on 
daily basis as and when necessity arose. He has not worked continuously for 240 days in a calendar year. This 
witness in his cross-examination has also stated that no attendance register was maintained by the branch with 


544 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JANUARY 24, 2026/MAGHA 4, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 
regard to the attendance of workman. 


13. In this case, non-production of the above said record by the respondent-bank as asked by the workman was 
not necessary as there was no record of the workman with the bank. Moreover, workman is having best evidence 
with him in the shape of his bank account where his salary was deposited by the bank which he has not produced in 
the Tribunal. Thus, rather adverse inference can be drawn against the workman. 


14. In his written argument, the workman has placed on record certain documents which are irrelevant for 
proving that workman had worked for 240 days preceding the year of his termination. These documents which he 
has attached with his written argument are not admissible in evidence because these documents were never exhibited 
by the workman in his statement or by calling any other person. 


15. It is entirely for workman to prove the completion of 240 days of his service with the respondent-bank prior 
to his retrenchment and onus to prove this fact is always on the workman which the workman has failed to prove it. 
Thus, protection under Section 25-F of the Act is not available to the workman. 


16. In view of my findings on the above discussed issues as discussed in the preceding paragraphs, this 
reference is decided against the workman. 


17. Let copy of this award be sent to Central Government for publication as required under Section 17 of the 
Act. 


KAMAL KANT, Presiding Officer

AWARD 


By order No. L-41011/89/2013(R(B-I)) Dated: 13.11.2013, the present industrial dispute has been referred 
for adjudication in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section (1) and sub-section (2A) of Section 
10 the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947) by the Central Government, with following schedule: 


“क्या प्रबंधना TR रेलवे लखनऊ EAT श्री सर्बदुरहमान को दिए गए GST विनाक 06/05/2008 F अपीनीय आदेश 
दि०06/08/2008 Ft RET किया जाना न्यायोचित एवं बैध हैं? यदि नहीं तो at किस राहत को पाने का हकदार हैं?" 


Accordingly, था 1.12. Case No. 71/2013 has been registered. 


On 27.01.2014, workman filed a claim statement fact in brief as stated by him that are he was engaged as substitute 
cleaner by respondent, while he was working in a said capacity a medical memo issued to him for medical 
examination to which he filed his objection. 


Aggrieved by the said facts a charge sheet dated 17.03.2007, issued to him as per para 514(F) of India Railway 
Medical Manual-2000 Volume-I., to which he submitted his reply on 08.03.2008. 


Thereafter on 05.05.2008, a punishment was awarded to him, aggrieved by the same he preferred an appeal dismissed 
by order dated 06.08.2008. 


Accordingly it is prayed by the workman that the impugned punishment order dated 05.05.2008, and appellate order 
dated 06.08.2008, may be set aside, and he may be reinstated in service. 


On behalf of the respondent a written statement was filed to which the workman has filed his reply. 
Thereafter the workman file evidence in support of his case affidavit/examination in chief on 05.09.2016(W7). 


In spite of the repeat opportunity given to him he refused/did not turn up to get him cross examined on his 
examination in chief, filed by way of evidence on affidavit. 


So by order dated 29.06.2018, this Tribunal has closed the right of his cross examine. 
Thereafter management/respondent filed its evidence on affidavit. 


In spite of the opportunity given to the worker, he did not cross examine the management witness, so the same was 
closed. 


On 19.01.2021; matter was fixed for hearing, since then the case is lingering due to delay on the part of the workman, 
as he has not put his appearance in person or through its legal representation to argue the matter. 


Keeping in view the above said facts, this is a case of no evidence because worker did not cross examined himself on 
the evidence filed by him on affidavit (examination in chief) so the same in not proved as per the relevant provision 
Evidence Act, so keeping the said facts and the law as laid by the Hon'ble High Court in the case of V. K. Raj 
Industries v. Labour Court (1) and others 1981 (29) FLR 194 as under: 


"Tt is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove illegality 
of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail Whenever a 
workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative for him to file 
written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is challenged and he must 
also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file written statement or produce 
evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in favour of the workman and he 
would not be entitled to any relief." 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees' Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding 
Officer, Labour Court (ID, Ghaziabad and others 2008 (118) FLR 1164 Hon'ble Allahabad High Court has held 
as under: 


"The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., V.K. Raj 
Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1984 (49) FLR 38 and 
Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led by or on behalf of the 


546 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JANUARY 24, 2026/MAGHA 4, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In such a situation it is not 
necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead evidence to establish an allegation 
made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, who would fail if no evidence is led." 


And by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co- operative Bank Ltd. 2010 (126) FLR 519; wherein it has been held 
as under: 


"The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the shoulders of the 
respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead evidence first which he failed. A 
perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence either oral or documentary was led by the 
respondent. In the case of no evidence, the reference has to be dismissed." 


AWARD 
For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 
Award as above. 
Lucknow.
